ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $ \angle MON=35^\circ$, point P is on the side $ ON$ of $ \angle MON$. With point P as the center and $ PO$ as the radius, an arc is drawn, intersecting $ OM$ at point A. When $ AP$ is connected, what is the degree measure of $ \angle APN$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} From the diagram, we know that $PO=PA$,\\
$\therefore \angle PAO = \angle O = 35^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle APN = \angle O + \angle PAO = \boxed{70^\circ}$.

method.method_draft: First describe the diagram: O, P, N lie on the same horizontal ray with P between O and N; OM is the slanted upper ray of angle MON; A lies on OM and is also on the arc centered at P; segment AP is drawn. From the text/construction, the arc has center P and radius PO, so PA = PO. In triangle OPA, this makes it isosceles with base OA. Since OA lies along OM and OP lies along ON, angle POA is the given angle MON, 35°. Therefore the base angle PAO is also 35°. Use the exterior angle theorem at P: angle APN is the exterior angle of triangle OPA formed by extending PO to PN, so angle APN = angle POA + angle PAO = 35° + 35° = 70°.
